rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words - grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: derive-body-view.js grep banned_words (delve|honest|importantly|crucial|substrate|synergize|paradigm shift) body_hits = 0, planted_proof true; leverage_verb body_hits = 0, planted_proof true; em_dash body_hits = 0, planted_proof true. Independently re-run: awk '/^<!-- maintainer -->/{exit} /—/{print NR}' returned empty. Closest call is L5 'This capability unlocks transformational value' - 'unlock' is consultancy register but not on the §1 list; it is filed under §13 instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony - hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: derive-body-view.js grep ritual_ceremony body_hits = 0, planted_proof true. No practice(n) in body either; nearest register noun is L13 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: derive-body-view.js greps dated_line body_hits = 0 and session_biography body_hits = 0, both planted_proof true. No transition verb in body lines 1-65; the tense test finds only present-state prose. (Maintainer-block journey clauses are out of body scope - see notes.)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: prose in the wrong register for the AE101 voice quintet, which flinches an engineer audience. Present. Three body lines are marketing/consultancy register, none of the five voices: L5 'This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.' (growth-hack 'unlocks' + abstraction, and the AE101 audience contract's flinch-grep territory), L37 'Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.' (competitive-positioning register), L49 'We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.' (brand-manifesto register). None sells a defensible approval, relocates an engineering virtue, or names a payoff in the reader's currency.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut all three; the surrounding beats already carry the teaching, and no quintet voice is missing if they go.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule's author-we sub-rule prevents: first-person-plural body prose speaking as the training-as-organisation, which is the creator-name failure one step abstracted. Present at L49: 'We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.' Substitution diagnostic: 'the training authors believe the loop matters more than the model, and the training authors built this training around that' - reads exactly as author-we, not as the student+Claude collective, not a quoted team voice, not the framed-memoir carve-out. Mechanical: derive-body-view.js grep author_we body_hits = 1, planted_proof true, and it resolves to this line. No creator-name hit ('Antti' appears only at L72, below the maintainer cut).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the sentence; the loop-over-model stance is already carried by the exercise's own moves and by L13's point line.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: derive-body-view.js grep the_student body_hits = 0, planted_proof true. Body is consistently second person ('the bug you fixed', L17). No delivery mechanics in body; the trainer moves all sit below the cut at L86-L92.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a term-of-art landing in body with no earning moment, so the reader meets a word the curriculum never gave them. Present at L11: 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' 'compaction boundary' has no earning moment in this file and none upstream in the body of this exercise; 'subagent' likewise is never landed here. The maintainer accept-note at L72 covers exactly one term ('connector') and explicitly no others, so this is not a pre-accepted passage. Distinct from the AE101 commonly-known-LLM-vocabulary carve-out in §4: 'context window' is legal working vocabulary, 'compaction boundary' is Claude Code runtime shorthand that only appears in maintainer/platform surfaces.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the line; nothing downstream depends on it, and no beat in this exercise runs a subagent or approaches compaction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line is L30 'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works. One the agent just wrote carries none of your team's conventions.' That is an alternative path plus its reason, not reassurance about the reader's standing - it carries none of the flag shapes (no penalty / fine way to / it's OK if / you are not on the hook for). Stays inside.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L24 'Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.' is the only slogan-shaped body line, and §21 routes it away from here: §12's remedy presupposes a claim that holds broadly, and this one has no true reading. Judged under §21 below rather than shoehorned into a downstream-carve-out fix.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: the curriculum's positioning posture imported into a teaching beat, which reads defensive and marketing-shaped to an engineer. Present twice, and the hard sub-rule fires on the second. L5: 'This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.' - value-prop claim about the training, in a slot that owes the reader the exercise's contract. L37: 'Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.' - matches the rule's flag list ('unlike consultancy decks' shape) and trips the hard sub-rule verbatim: treat 'vendor' in student-facing body as suspect every time. The narrow Agents 101 M7 taxonomy exception does not reach this file. L49's brand-manifesto sentence is the same leak and is filed under §6 as author-we.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut L5 and L37 outright; the beat that follows each is the teaching and neither sentence sets it up.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: operational copy lifting vocabulary the student has not reached, pre-spoiling the module that owns it. Present at L11 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' - this sits in the opening widget region of an M1 exercise (third of four, per the maintainer block at L70), where the arc's current vocabulary is tickets, trackers and the agent. 'subagent' and 'compaction boundary' are both ahead of this arc position, and this is a lead-in-register line, exactly the operational surface the rule guards.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Same cut as §8; if a compaction note is wanted at all it belongs where the training actually earns it, not in an M1 tracker exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the sub-clause prevents (pronoun/referent check, explicitly NOT post-trim-gated - it fires on any closer): a demonstrative the reader cannot resolve cold. Present at L11 'Wire this through the subagent context window' - 'this' has no antecedent. The preceding line L9 is the '**What you build:**' widget (bug rules and a close-out note) and the following line L13 is '**The point:**'; nothing in either is a thing one wires through a context window. Read cold, the reader cannot point at what 'this' is or at what action 'wire through' names.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence (§8/§14 say the same); if any part survives, name the concrete noun instead of 'this'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL - default is to omit it
rules_evaluated.evidence: L60-L62 include the recap as a `## What happened` section and it holds the three moves: count + noun ('Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along.'), one qualifier ('your team has been encoding in its fields all along'), and past tense throughout ('came out', 'you shipped', 'closed'). 43 words, above the 25-40 band but not a replay of the step sequence. The forward sentence at L64 is filed under check_student_facing §33, not here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No bark/order/command/whip/force/drag/boss verb in lines 1-65. Closest is L39 'Push back on the five.' - push-back is the house peer-flat move, not a combative verb aimed at the agent, and the rest of the body uses ask/tell/open/paste.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat - the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No deictic drumroll, no bold-label echo (no bolded handles in body at all, consistent with the emphasis-budget note at L78), no citation duplication. Closest is the empty-negation test on L29 'One ticket gives a sample of your team's rules, not the policy.' - the reader's actual prior IS that one ticket shows the policy, so the negation is doing work and stays.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The only numerals in body are 'five bug rules' (L33 lead-in) and 'the five' (L39). Neither sits above a list the reader can see: the five rules are output the agent will produce inside the prompt, so the numeral is the handle the reader carries forward, which is the rule's own carve-out. The four bullets at L28-L31 carry no count sentence above them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing - run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a memorable line with no true reading shipping as design stance, where a professional audience finds the counterexample faster than the author. Present at L24: 'Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.' Superlative is the tell ('never'), and the claim is asserted about how the world works, not scoped to an artifact we control. Counterexamples are immediate and this file supplies one: the agent in this very exercise edits the repo and could edit or delete a test, and the exercise's own upstream beat (`fix-tests-first`, named at L70) is built on a test that was failing. The line is also unowned by the backing block at L113-L142, which is where §21 says these survive.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the line rather than hedge it - 'usually the only' is worse. If a claim about tests is wanted here, scope it to what the tests actually guard.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every body string quoted by the `<!-- backing -->` claim ledger still resolves in the body I read. Verified by awk index() on the raw source: 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules' -> L13; 'Every field carries a convention.' -> L28; 'One ticket gives a sample of your team's rules, not the policy.' -> L29; 'The ones you reject sharpen the read as much as the ones you keep.' -> L39; 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM' -> L57. No missing quotes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line is L53 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.' The observation named is the comments already on the ticket - an external artifact that can come back negative - not the close-out judging itself. No self-witnessing instrument in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap or tier-pegging phrasing. Closest is L30 'No ticket of your own to read?' which describes a setup fact, not a deficiency, and no identity criterion is handed over anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a cold term stopping the reader mid-narrative. Present at L11 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' - narrative prose, not a legend or an index, so the scan carve-out does not reach it. Checked the file's maintainer block first per the 2026-08-18 carve-out: the accept-note at L72 rules 'connector' assumed-known and names only that term; 'compaction boundary' is not industry-standard vocabulary an AE101 engineer owns from working life, it is Claude Code runtime shorthand. 'subagent' is a Claude Code primitive with no operational landing anywhere in this exercise.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the line; there is no beat here for the terms to be earned against.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body - THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two recoveries sit in body and both pass the base test (plausible failure + non-obvious rescue, one tight line): L18 'If there is no ticket for this bug, say so in the chat. The agent will offer to create one.' and L30 'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works.' Routing either below the fence would delete it, per the stripMaintainerTail mechanism the rule names. No pre-emptive FAQ beyond these.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the third-axis clause prevents: a line that reads as an instruction but names no doable move, so the student cannot tell whether they executed it. Present at L11 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' - who does this, and through what? No actor, no mechanism, no artifact; 'wire through' names a manner, not a move, and nothing in the exercise produces a thing to wire. The register beat at L53 is clean by contrast: it names the object (the comments already on the ticket), the tell (wording that feels off), the actor and the addressee ('tell Claude which line').
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut L11. Its neighbours (L9 and L13) join cleanly without it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: awk '/^<!-- maintainer -->/{exit} /—/{print NR}' on the raw source returned no lines; derive-body-view.js em_dash grep body_hits = 0 with planted_proof true. Sentences are short; the longest body sentence is L57 and it is a colon-led list, not a nest of sub-clauses.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four of six section headers lead with a verb: 'Read the ticket for your bug' (L15), 'Read the conventions off the ticket' (L26), 'Write the close-out and send it' (L41), 'Double-check the voice' (L51). Closest to failing is L55 'Anything can be reverse-engineered', declarative over a section whose second bullet is an instruction - it stays inside because the section's job is the generalisation itself (the claim the backing block registers as the maintainer-attested frame), with the instruction trailing it. 'What happened' (L60) is the canonical recap name.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: One inline link, L43: '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' - link text is the target's title, not a filename and not a backticked code-span path. No ordinal cross-references anywhere in body ('the bug you fixed', 'the next exercise', never 'Step 4'). Path form is governed elsewhere; see notes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The split holds through the body: acting -> 'the agent' (L18 'The agent will offer to create one.', L29, L58 'Ask the agent to study the pipeline'); addressee -> 'Claude' (L33 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer', L45, L53); capability/thinking -> 'LLM' (L57 'inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM'). Body counts run agent-heavy, not Claude-heavy, so no assistant-shaped framing signal.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No noun-run in body. 'session' is used correctly for the sitting at L43 ('it pays back on every session after this one') and L64 ('sweeps this whole session'); no 'this run', no 'the run' for the agent's sitting.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: body clauses that change nothing the student understands, decides, does or notices next. Present four times, and the fastest screen (is this obvious to a working engineer, or does it change what they do?) kills all four: L5 'This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.' changes no next move; L11 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' names no move at all; L37 'Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.' is positioning; L49 'We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.' is maintainer rationale in body. Delete all four and every neighbouring pair joins cleanly.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut all four lines. None is a candidate for relocation below the fence - the maintainer block already carries the reasoning worth keeping.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a forward-looking aside whose grammatical subject is the training rather than the student, which reads as value-prop. Failure mode (a), present at L49: 'We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.' Subject is the training authors and then the training itself; the student appears nowhere in the sentence. Same line is filed under §6 (author-we) and §13 - three rules, one sentence, which is what makes it worth deleting rather than recasting.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete rather than recast to 'you'; recasting would preserve a claim about the training that the beat does not need.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself - subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: maintainer cartography reaching the student, and specifically the 2026-08-23 predicate leak - a clause promising what a later beat will do is cartography however the sentence starts. Present at L64: 'The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' First sentence passes on both subject and predicate and should stay; the second states another exercise's job and is a cheque that beat must cash. This section is `## What happened`, not one of the exempt signposting sections (`## Bridge` / `## Next` / `## Prework`). Deletion test: the two survive as 'The field rules stay in the scrollback.' with nothing lost. L49 is the same leak in its other direction and is filed under §28.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the second sentence of L64; the maintainer Arc note at L104 already records the hand-off for whoever needs it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read the expanded view (curriculum/evals/body-views/shared--file--writing-5judge.expanded.md, signals.has_prompt_blocks true). No bracketed slot in any of the three fences. close-the-ticket-1 uses the open-hook shape correctly - internal action paragraphs first, single 'Ticket:' line last (expanded L29) - and the student genuinely holds the value (their own ticket), so the qualifier is satisfied.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three markers carry a command-verb lead-in under 20 words and none is mechanical narration: L20 'Drop the ticket link after the colon.' (7 words - the §2a dangling-colon sub-case, where naming the input is the lead-in's whole job, and it correctly carries no summary in front of it), L33 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs and propose five bug rules.' (14), L45 'Ask Claude to write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote.' (14). Closest to §2a bloat is L45 against a 4-clause 55-word fence, which the rule explicitly allows a fuller lead-in for.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one side-effecting prompt (close-the-ticket-3, a ticket update) closes on post-action report, not pre-confirm: expanded L68 ends 'Tell me what you wrote.' and the body lead-in at L45 mirrors it ('report what it wrote'). A tracker comment is correctable after the fact, so the irreversible-action carve-out does not apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three prompts are registry-sourced markers on their own line - {{prompt:close-the-ticket-1}} L22, -2 L35, -3 L47 - and all three registry files exist (ls curriculum/prompts/ | grep close-the-ticket returns close-the-ticket-1.md, close-the-ticket-2.md, close-the-ticket-3.md). Naming follows <file-slug>-<n>. No inline **Prompt** block in source.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rhyme holds on each pair in the expanded view: L41 'Ask Claude to reverse-engineer how your team handles bugs' against fence opening 'Reverse-engineer how this team handles bugs from one bug ticket.' (same verb, same noun phrase); L63 'write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote' against 'Update the ticket: short close-out note ... Tell me what you wrote.' The first pair is the dangling-colon case where §2a deliberately replaces the summary, so no mirror is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a draft flattening the module's deliberate mood. AE101 M1's target is earned trust, and this is a teaching beat, not mechanical setup, so the mood floor applies. The three marketing-register lines (L5, L37, L49) each swap earned trust for asserted value - a reader who has not yet closed a single ticket is told the capability is transformational, that the approach beats vendor tooling, and what the training believes. That is the signature wrong-edit for a trust-building beat: claiming the payoff before the student has produced the evidence. The beats themselves (read one real ticket, reverse-engineer the fields, write the close-out) carry the mood correctly once those three lines are gone.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cutting L5, L37 and L49 restores the mood; no positive addition is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section headers name disciplines and moves, never failure words: 'Read the conventions off the ticket' (L26), 'Write the close-out and send it' (L41), 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' (L55). The point line at L13 names a capability ('the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules'), not a defect.

findings.quote: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.
findings.harm: Value-prop copy in a teaching slot. Sells the payoff before the student has produced any evidence for it, in a register no AE101 voice speaks, and changes nothing the reader does next.
findings.fix: Cut the line. The '**What you do:**' and '**What you build:**' widgets on either side already state the contract.

findings.quote: Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.
findings.harm: Competitive positioning imported into a teaching beat, and a bare 'vendor' in student-facing body, which the hard sub-rule says to treat as suspect every time. Reads defensive to engineers who would rather read the citation and decide.
findings.fix: Cut the line. It sits between the five-rules prompt and the push-back paragraph and connects neither.

findings.quote: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
findings.harm: First-person-plural body prose speaking as the training-as-organisation - the creator-name failure one step abstracted, and the forward-callout subject test's failure mode (a). Substituting 'the training authors' for 'we' makes the sentence read as exactly what it is.
findings.fix: Delete rather than recast. Recasting to second person would preserve a claim about the training that the beat does not need.

findings.quote: Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.
findings.harm: Four faults in one sentence: an unearned term of art ('compaction boundary'), vocabulary ahead of this arc position ('subagent'), a demonstrative with no antecedent ('this'), and no actor or mechanism - the student cannot perform it or tell whether they did. The maintainer accept-note at L72 covers 'connector' only.
findings.fix: Cut the line. L9 and L13 join cleanly without it, and nothing downstream in the exercise runs a subagent or approaches compaction.

findings.quote: Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.
findings.harm: A superlative asserted about how the world works, with no true reading. The agent edits this repo and can edit or delete a test; the upstream exercise this one follows is built on a test that was failing. A carve-out under §12 would leave a false sentence standing with a hedge bolted on.
findings.fix: Cut it. Hedging to 'usually' is worse than the original - the surrounding beat carries the point without it.

findings.quote: The next exercise sweeps this whole session.
findings.harm: A clause promising what a later beat will do is cartography however the sentence starts, and it is a cheque that beat has to cash. `## What happened` is not one of the exempt signposting sections.
findings.fix: Keep 'The field rules stay in the scrollback.' and cut the second sentence; the maintainer Arc note at L104 already records the hand-off.

todos.note: Register: three body lines (L5, L37, L49) sit outside the AE101 voice quintet in marketing/consultancy register. Resolved by the cuts above; no rewrite owed.
Jargon planted ahead of arc position ('subagent', 'compaction boundary') in an M1 exercise. Resolved by cutting L11.
Dangling demonstrative: 'Wire this through' has no antecedent in L9 or L13. Resolved by cutting L11.
False-as-stated slogan; cut rather than hedge.
'compaction boundary' is unearned and is not audience-assumed-known; the L72 accept-note names 'connector' only.
Not executable: no actor, no mechanism, no way for the student to tell they did it.
NVA sweep: L5, L11, L37, L49 all fail the does-this-change-what-the-student-does screen.
Forward-callout subject is the training, not the student. Delete rather than recast.
Later-beat predicate in the recap; cut the second sentence.
M1 earned-trust mood flattened by the three asserted-value lines; the cuts restore it.

notes: derive-class-brief.js built cleanly: 129 rules across check_writing.md (26), check_student_facing.md (35), check_prompts.md (48), check_sales_copy.md (13), check_strategy_tie_in.md (7), 0 dropped, no prefill. Read the assembled brief in full rather than the five compendiums. Body region taken from derive-body-view.js, not re-derived: maintainer_cut = 66, fence_ranges = [], body = lines 1-65. Read the precomputed expanded projection because signals.has_prompt_blocks was true. Per the dispatch instruction this is a scoped report, not an N/A ledger: rules with nothing to say about this body carry no row. check_sales_copy.md (13 rules) is out of surface scope entirely - this is a student-facing exercise, not buyer-facing copy - so it carries no rows at all; its em-dash and jargon bans are covered here by check_writing §1 and check_student_facing §14. Out-of-lane observations, not filed as verdicts: (a) the maintainer accept-note at L72 says the connector term sits at 'its line-35 use' but the link is at L43 - a stale locator inside a maintainer block, out of writing-class body scope, worth a maintainer fix under check_writing §3's keep-notes-bind clause; (b) the L43 link path carries a depth-counted '../' prefix, which curriculum/module-shape.md § Cross-doc links forbids - that is path form, governed outside this class, and check_student_facing §18 governs only the link text, which is correct; (c) six of the six body sections would each be one slide, which is check_slides.md's lane. Five of the six findings concentrate in four inserted-looking sentences (L5, L11, L37, L49) plus L24; L64 is the one that reads as pre-existing prose. No file other than the instance JSON was written.
